justifications.functional_suitability: Requirements R-01 through R-04 are largely met via Consultation Controller, Prescription Manager, Symptom Checker UI Module, and Consent & Policy Engine. However, the direct execution and orchestration of the AI Inference Engine is missing an explicit backend mediating component.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Open Policy Agent (PDP) provides low-latency authorization, and asynchronous publishing is used in Audit & Traceability Publisher. However, concrete mechanisms for caching, request queuing, or handling degraded video below 300 kbit/s beyond externalizing to the SFU are not detailed.
justifications.compatibility: Prescription Manager connects to Regional Pharmacy Gateways supporting HL7 FHIR and national EU APIs. Video Infrastructure Provider leverages WebRTC and SRTP/DTLS, while Identity & Consent Providers standardizes on OIDC/OAuth2 and FIDO2/WebAuthn.
justifications.usability: All target personas are covered: Patients via Patient Portal App (Flutter), Clinicians via Clinician Workspace App (React SPA), and Compliance Officers via API Gateway / BFF accessing reports generated by Export Formatter.
justifications.reliability: Degraded mode below 300 kbit/s (R-06) is relegated to external SFU descriptions without concrete adaptive bitrate or audio-only fallback logic in Consultation View Controller. High availability, multi-region failover, and fault-tolerance mechanisms are absent.
justifications.security: Enforces ABAC via Consent & Policy Engine (OPA PDP), mTLS with SPIFFE/SPIRE via gRPC Client Proxy, and immutability via WORM storage in Audit & Traceability Publisher. Data residency is addressed logically in Prescription Data Access.
justifications.maintainability: Clear modular separation of concerns between API Gateway / BFF, Consultation & Prescriptions Service, and AI Traceability & Logging Service using defined interfaces (GraphQL Federation, gRPC). Components within containers exhibit high cohesion.
justifications.portability: The required multi-region GCP deployment (europe-west3 and us-central1) to enforce strict EU/US residency is completely omitted from the architecture model. Standard containerized runtimes are used, but environment mapping is missing.

PERF-01.justification: Signaling is handled by high-performance Go/gRPC services and GraphQL BFF, while media streaming is offloaded to an external WebRTC SFU. However, reliance on a third-party SFU introduces external latency risks during sudden traffic spikes.
tradeoffs: Offloading media to third-party SFU reduces server load but sacrifices direct latency control

PERF-02.justification: While 50,000 requests/hour (~14 req/s) is light for the FastAPI logging service and BFF, third-party LLM inference latency frequently exceeds 3 s without explicit asynchronous streaming, caching, or localized inference endpoints.
sensitivity_points: External LLM latency and queueing times
tradeoffs: External LLM flexibility versus unpredictable tail latency under load

AVAIL-01.justification: The external WebRTC SFU specifically addresses low-bandwidth degradation, and the mobile/web clients support offline caching to prevent consultation note loss during network drops.
tradeoffs: Degrading video stream quality preserves connection stability and clinical note capture

AVAIL-02.justification: Target cloud lists only us-central1 and europe-west3. Since US patient data cannot legally move to the EU, an outage of us-central1 without a secondary US failover region or documented regional DR mechanism prevents recovery within 1 hour.
sensitivity_points: Availability of secondary cloud regions within the US
tradeoffs: Strict regional residency prevents cross-region DR failover to the EU region

MOD-01.justification: Prescription Manager interacts with Regional Pharmacy Gateways using national APIs, but lacks an explicitly defined adapter or plug-in layer within the container components to isolate national protocol changes to a single modular unit.
sensitivity_points: Coupling within Prescription Manager for different national formats
tradeoffs: Consolidated prescription service simplifies deployment but risks code churn during regional extensions

MOD-02.justification: The AI Traceability & Logging Service features dedicated audit processors to ingest and record model metadata and inferences for EU MDR traceability. Model rollback mechanics depend on the external AI Inference Engine configuration.
sensitivity_points: Inference request payload schema capturing model version IDs
tradeoffs: Decoupled inference logging ensures regulatory traceability but requires coordination with external engines

SEC-01.justification: The architecture incorporates a Policy Decision Point using Open Policy Agent for fine-grained ABAC and purpose-based consent evaluation. All decisions and cross-border access attempts are published asynchronously to immutable WORM storage.
sensitivity_points: Completeness of OPA policy rules for cross-border access
tradeoffs: Sub-millisecond ABAC checks add micro-latency to all cross-border data requests

SEC-02.justification: Consent updates in the Consent & Policy Engine take immediate effect at the Policy Decision Point, preventing subsequent reads for research purposes well within 24 hours. Verification is supported via the Audit & Traceability Publisher.
sensitivity_points: PDP cache invalidation latency after consent withdrawal
Audit log queryability for compliance verification
tradeoffs: Immediate authorization invalidation increases policy lookup traffic to the consent store
